summary: Tenant-level optimizer harmonization support and safe rollback after mixed-profile anomalies
description:
Issue summary: CloudScribe (dedicated tenant) reported divergent text outputs and intermittent p95 latency spikes after a tenant-scoped optimizer rollout that combined a new quantization profile with an aggressive batching policy and KV prefetch tweaks. The customer attempted to revert the change via the console but observed mixed-model behaviour and some requests still routed to a quantized variant, causing both quality drift and tail latency.

Impact: Several production routes for CloudScribe show increased 95th- and 99th-percentile latency (from baseline ~120ms p95 to 480-650ms p95) and two customer-facing services report a small but measurable quality regression on generation prompts (token-level repeats and truncated completions). Traffic is ~300 rps for the tenant in us-west. No data exfiltration suspected; logs show increased cache evictions and recompile events.

Environment: prod - us-west (CloudScribe dedicated pool), affected models: redwood-v2-8B and fallback open-llama-7B. Router config indicates per-tenant optimizer flags were applied via an audit script on 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Send representative prompt set from CloudScribe test harness; 2) Observe occasional output truncation and repeat tokens on a subset (~8-12%) of responses; 3) Query runtime /metrics and dashboard for p95/p99 latency and cache evictions.

Observed behavior: Mixed routing where ~30% of requests land on quantized variant with observed decoding anomalies; p95 spikes correlate with increased KV cache misses and GC/recompile activity on specific GPU nodes. Attempts to toggle the tenant optimizer flag in Console returned success but the router cache showed stale entries for some nodes.

Expected behavior: A console toggle/rollback should be atomic for tenant-scoped optimizer changes and routing should consistently respect the rollback within 60s. Quality should return to baseline when quantized variant is fully disabled.

Logs/metrics references: Dashboards: /dashboards/tenants/cloudscribe/optimizer-telemetry (snapshot 2026-03-10T05:20Z). Kibana traces: trace IDs and sample request IDs provided in comments. SRE runbook referenced: Tenant Optimizer Runbook (Confluence link included).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Support (Asha): Acknowledged. Opening investigation and cc'ing Runtime and SRE. SLAs noted.
2026-03-10 09:45 UTC - Runtime Eng (Diego): Can you attach a sample request ID where output truncated? Also need the tenant's optimizer snapshot version. Added INT-4021 to check router cache state.

2026-03-10 10:02 UTC - Customer (CloudScribe - Priya Rao): Provided request IDs: rq_00123, rq_00176, rq_00201 and optimizer snapshot 2026-03-09-03:12:07. We attempted Console rollback at 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC but saw intermittent results.

2026-03-11 01:20 UTC - SRE (Marta): Observed elevated cache evictions on nodes gpu-wst-07 and gpu-wst-09 coincident with deploy. Recompile spike on runtime pods pointed out. Investigating memory pressure and kernel selection fallback.

2026-03-12 14:05 UTC - Support (Asha): Proposed safe plan: 1) Quarantine tenant to dedicated routing gate, 2) Disable optimizer flags for the tenant from control plane, 3) Perform staged traffic split to fallback model, 4) Restore tenant snapshot if needed. Customer approved maintenance window 2026-03-13 02:00-03:00 UTC.

2026-03-13 02:10 UTC - Runtime Eng (Diego): Started staged traffic split to 80/20 -> 50/50. Observed p95 drop to ~210ms at 50/50 in us-west. Some requests still showing quantized variant; router cache invalidation routine triggered.
2026-03-14 08:33 UTC - Support (Asha): Following up to request post-rollback diff reports and to schedule a post-mortem if quality regression persists.
investigation_notes: Telemetry: p95 jumped from 120ms -> 480-650ms after flag application. KV cache miss rate increased by 3x. Recompile events observed correlated with the optimizer rollout timestamp.
Hypothesis 1: Mixed optimizer profiles across pool nodes caused inconsistent kernel selection and cache incompatibilities leading to recompile thrashing and evictions.
Hypothesis 2: Router did not fully invalidate per-tenant routing cache; some nodes continued to serve an older quantized variant pinned in local state.

Evidence: Node-level logs (gpu-wst-07) show repeated model_recompile and tensor_format_mismatch warnings between 03:12-03:45 UTC on 2026-03-09. Console audit shows a partially successful rollback operation at 02:10 UTC on 2026-03-11 with 'stale-cache' warnings.
Temporary mitigation attempted: Manual router cache invalidation (script ID rc_invalidate_2026_03_13) and staged traffic split. p95 improved at 50/50 but full recovery not yet achieved.
Cross-links: INT-4021 (router cache tooling ticket) and SUP-82765 (similar tenant rollback assisted last month).
resolution_notes: 1) Execute deterministic per-tenant snapshot restore: created snapshot restore job cloudscribe-snap-20260309 and queued with high priority.
2) Disable optimizer flags for CloudScribe at control-plane layer and ensure gateway-level override to force fallback model routing.
3) Run a full router cache invalidation across the dedicated pool and add a short TTL to prevent stale entries (patch submitted: control-plane PR 989).
4) Perform final staged traffic rampdown of quantized variant (50/50 -> 10/90 -> 0/100) during low-traffic window, monitoring p95/p99 and output diffs.
- Add a console guardrail: require router cache invalidation confirmation before marking tenant rollback as complete.
- Add telemetry alert: simultaneous rise in recompile events + KV eviction rate to auto-trigger an optimizer rollback recommendation.
- SRE to audit memory/driver logs on gpu-wst-07 and gpu-wst-09 and rotate nodes if hardware-induced kernel selection instability is found.

Status: Partial mitigation applied (router invalidation + 50/50 traffic split). Next steps scheduled for 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC: complete snapshot restore and full rollback. Customer will be kept informed and a post-mortem will be drafted if quality regression persists after full rollback.
